purpose: Define an explicit calorically-perfect effective-gas policy for the present quasi-one-dimensional solver. The policy preserves the NASA source vitiated-stream composition, derives R_mix from species molecular weights, derives cp_mix and gamma_eff at the 1270 K NASA inlet reference state from public NASA7 species polynomials, and requires temperature-sensitivity reporting. It is a reduced-order model assumption, not a claim that the reacting mixture has constant gamma throughout the combustor.

thermo_source.citation: Cantera gri30.yaml documentation, GRI-Mech Version 3.0 thermodynamics in NASA7 CHEMKIN-II polynomial format.
thermo_source.coefficient_selection: Use the high-temperature coefficient interval because T_ref=1270 K > 1000 K.

constants.molecular_weight_policy: O2=2*15.999, H2O=2*1.008+15.999, N2=2*14.007; standard atomic weights are used only to evaluate ideal-gas species R_i.

formal_case_policy.required_sensitivity: A formal NASA-BK reduced-order result must report sensitivity to at least one lower gamma representative of the heated range; the reference-state constant-gamma run alone is not sufficient for a robustness claim.
scope_boundary: The composition is held at the NASA vitiated inlet composition when evaluating the effective-gas properties.
Chemical composition changes caused by hydrogen combustion are not represented in gamma or R.
The NASA7 cp(T) data are used to quantify the constant-gamma approximation; the production solver still uses a calorically perfect gas in each run.
This closure is suitable only for a reduced-order thermal/flow validation claim, not finite-rate chemistry or species validation.
